title: Cohort-based KV segmentation throughput and p95 regression harness
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Purpose: Build a reproducible load-testing harness that evaluates KV/prefix-cache behavior under cohort-segmented workloads. Each cohort represents a distinct access pattern (short-tail heavy, broad long-tail, spike-bursts, and steady-state). The harness will measure tokens/sec throughput, p95 latency, and memory occupancy across segments; detect regressions against baseline profiles; and produce artifacts consumable by CI and the console dashboards.
motivation: Existing KV tests treat traffic as a single homogeneous distribution. Real customer workloads contain multiple cohorts with different locality and TTL properties. Small regressions (1-3% p95) in a hot cohort can cause visible customer regressions even when aggregate metrics look stable. This harness isolates cohorts to surface such regressions and attributes them to cache hit-rate, eviction churn, or GC/memory pressure.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can generate at least four configurable cohorts concurrently with independent request distributions. 2) For each run, produce a time-series CSV containing tokens/sec, p95, p50, hit_rate, evictions_per_min, resident_memory_mb sampled at 1s granularity. 3) Regression detector flags when p95 degrades >3% or hit_rate drops >2% for any cohort relative to baseline. 4) CI job integrates with GitHub Actions and fails when regression flags are raised. 5) Results are linked to a console dashboard panel for visual inspection.
test_plan: - Implement workload generator module that reads cohort definitions from JSON files. - Create traffic orchestrator to drive sequences (steady, ramp, burst, spike). - Instrument runtime to emit per-cohort metrics via existing metrics tag (kvcache.cohort=<cohort>). - Baseline: run on stable commit X with 3 repeats to compute mean and 95% CI. - Regression detection: compare new runs against baseline using threshold rules and statistical t-test for confidence. - Smoke run in staging lane; full matrix run on dedicated performance pool.
work_items: - Build cohort workload spec and generator (Aisha). - Instrument metrics tags and verify tag propagation (Ethan). - Implement regression detector service in perf infra (SRE). - Add CI workflow and console wiring (DevEx). - Run baseline suite and store artifacts (Perf Eng).
environment: staging-perf-cluster (8x A100), perf-dedicated-pool, runtime-1.22 build. Local harness supports Dockerized runtime for developer iterations.
regression_detection_strategy: Baseline runs compute mean and standard deviation for each metric per cohort. Primary trigger: relative p95 increase >3% for any cohort AND absolute p95 increase >5ms. Secondary triggers: cohort hit_rate drop >2% or evictions_per_min increase >10%. For borderline cases run automated replays (3 additional runs) and apply paired t-test; CI fails only when p-value < 0.05 and effect size exceeds thresholds.
run_steps: 1) Check out perf branch and build runtime-1.22 image. 2) Upload cohort spec files to perf artifacts bucket. 3) Start orchestrator with concurrency matrix (cohort weights, qps per cohort). 4) Monitor metrics stream and ensure tags are present. 5) Wait for steady-state window (default 10 minutes) then collect samples. 6) Run regression detector against stored baseline. 7) Archive CSVs and upload dashboard snapshots.
expected_risks: - Tagging overhead could skew p95 at microsecond scale. - Baselines might be noisy on shared infra; dedicate nodes for baseline. - Memory measurement inconsistencies across kernel versions. Mitigation: isolate nodes, pin kernel for perf lanes, and normalize sampling windows.
notes: Keep cohort definitions small and descriptive. Start with 4 cohorts: hot-short, warm-moderate, cold-wide, bursty-spike. Use synthetic keys with realistic prefix entropy; include occasional long-tail noise to simulate real customers. Coordinate with SRE to reserve perf nodes during baseline runs.
results_placeholder: pending: first baseline scheduled 2025-03-02. Expected output: CSVs + dashboard snapshots + CI integration PR.
review_feedback: PM: ensure actionable labels and link to customer incidents where cohort pattern matched (INC-9831). Design: request small visual sample of per-cohort heatmap for console. Eng Lead: validate that per-request tagging won't add >0.5% median latency.
follow_up: If the harness surfaces a regression, create a triage playbook that maps metric deltas to likely root causes (eviction churn, KV shard imbalance, kernel memory pressure) and add reproducible min-repro scripts to the ticket. Consider adding an automated mitigations checklist (apply temporary per-cohort rate-limiting) to limit customer impact.
related_customers: AcmeSearch, FinSaaS (customer-reported tail latency correlated with hot-key churn)
communication_plan: Announce baseline results to perf@redwood, tag affected product owners, and add an entry to the weekly perf sync. Attach console link and PR for review.
implementation_notes: Prefer minimal-impact tagging via request header extension; use existing metric exporter to avoid adding new ingestion pipelines. Regression detector will be implemented as a standalone utility that reads CSVs and emits SARIF-like report for CI.
postmortem_requirements: If a regression is released to prod and traced back to a change uncovered by this harness, author a postmortem and link ENG-76109 as the originating detection ticket. Include timeline, root cause, and mitigation steps.
